html:
The Matsumoto sarin attack was a nerve gas attack on 27 June 1994 in the city of Matsumoto, central Japan, by members of Aum Shinrikyo. It killed eight people and hurt several hundred.

Cult members drove a truck with a heater and a fan into a residential area at night and released sarin vapour. The target was a group of judges who lived nearby and were about to rule on a land case against the cult. Windows were open on a hot night, and people in nearby flats and houses were poisoned.

The police first suspected a man who lived in the area, Yoshiyuki Kono, whose wife was left in a long coma. The press treated him as the likely culprit for months, and he was later cleared and apologised to. Only after the Tokyo subway attack in 1995 did investigators link Matsumoto to the cult.

It was the first use of sarin against civilians by a non-state group, and it was a trial run for the larger attack in the capital.
